title: WeMacro Bluetooth valid zero batch count underflows the encoded count
description:
COUNT advertises a minimum0 but the accepted batch encodes (uint32_t)count-1, turning0 into UINT32_MAX. This contradicts the bounded step-count contract and portable sibling minimum1. Set a correct minimum or define safe zero semantics before transmission and test zero/minimum/maximum encoding. Device execution was not measured. Next action: coordinator assigns a focused repair and relevant regression.

Imported from .factory/findings/active/FND-20261101215425-fa40-complete-full-repository-audit-008.json (category: functional, blocking: no).

outcome.summary: COUNT min 1 fixes the client-sent-0 path: indigo_property_copy_values clamps (not rejects) value/target to min (indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c:2192-2195). Clamping to 1 means (uint32_t)1 - 1 = 0, which is fine. But 0 can still reach the d: encoding at indigo_mac_drivers/focuser_wemacro_bt/indigo_focuser_wemacro_bt.m:440. The driver writes COUNT value = 0 on abort (:402), and the countdown decrements it to 0 when a batch finishes (:248); neither write touches number.target. indigo_property_copy_values only updates the items present in the request (indigo_bus.c:2177-2209). So a later partial X_RAIL_EXECUTE change that leaves out COUNT (for example LENGTH or SETTLE_TIME only, as indigo_change_number_property_1 or indigo_prop_tool sends) keeps value 0 and transmits (uint32_t)0 - 1 = 0xFFFFFFFF. That is the exact underflow this ticket names. The countdown then starts at 0, goes to -1 and never reaches == 0 (:253), so without BACK the property also stays BUSY. Required: encode the batch from the requested count, not from the residual countdown value. Before transmitting, set X_RAIL_EXECUTE_COUNT_ITEM->number.value = X_RAIL_EXECUTE_COUNT_ITEM->number.target and encode that value - 1. target is always >= 1: init sets it (indigo_bus.c:1777), copy_values clamps it, and abort/countdown never write it. The portable sibling does the same, indigo_drivers/focuser_wemacro/indigo_focuser_wemacro.c:534. Extend the test to cover this path: COUNT value left at 0 by abort/countdown, then a request without COUNT, and the encoded d must not underflow. The current test fails on the pre-fix source but checks only the textual minimum and the arithmetic of the expression. Version bump 0x02000005 and formatting are fine; no PROPERTIES.md change is needed (no property added or removed).

Re-review at 6d0fa41959. The underflow path from round 1 is closed. indigo_mac_drivers/focuser_wemacro_bt/indigo_focuser_wemacro_bt.m:440 now sets X_RAIL_EXECUTE_COUNT_ITEM->number.value = number.target just before the 0x10 command. target is always >= 1: init sets it, indigo_property_copy_values clamps it to min 1 (indigo_bus.c:2192-2195), and the abort (:402) and countdown (:248) writes never touch it. So a partial X_RAIL_EXECUTE request without COUNT, sent after abort or completion, now sends target - 1 and not 0xFFFFFFFF, and the countdown restarts from the requested count. This matches the portable sibling (indigo_focuser_wemacro.c:534 uses target). COUNT min 1 still covers the client-sent 0, which is clamped to 1 and encoded as 0. New test test_batch_start_uses_requested_count_after_countdown_left_zero compiles the real X_RAIL_EXECUTE handler body, extracted with driver_source_probe.body. It starts with value 0 and target in {1, 5, 0xFFFFFF}, stubs copy_values as a request that leaves COUNT out, and asserts the d sent equals target - 1 and the value equals target. Mutation check in a scratch copy, no source edit: with the added line removed, the probe fails (sent_d[1] = 0xFFFFFFFF); with it, the probe passes. DRIVER_VERSION 0x02000005 > 0x02000004. git diff --check is clean, the added line is one line with tab indentation, no README or PROPERTIES.md change is required, and whitespace/unit checks passed on this tree.
